2. Opposite party No.1, a firm engaged in exporting jute goods, as plaintiff on 13-5-2001 instituted the suit against the petitioner, a statutory corporation, and others for a decree for US$ 436,578.58 equivalent to Taka 24,011,821.90 as compensation with interest of Taka 3,814,265.39 for the period from 14-5-2000 to 30-4-2001 and also for further decree for damages of US $ 1,000,000 equivalent to Taka 55,000,000 against trading loss, US $ 2,000,000 equivalent to Taka 110,000,000 against international market loss and US $ 5,000,000 equivalent to Taka 275,000,000 against injury to health, causing mental agony and shortening of life expectancy, in total Taka 440,000,000. Plaintiff's offer being firm bid No. F 1431 dated 23-9-98 for 97,337 bales of jute goods was accepted by the Corporation with modified terms and conditions by its letter dated 29-9-98. Out of 97,337 bales, 95,504 bales were sacking and 1833 hessian. The contract dated 29-9-98 was made subject to BJMC's FOB/CNF standard Contract. One of the. conditions was that the Corporation would not sell standard B Twiils, cut size Twills and Binola B Twills to Sudan below 10,000 bales against any single offer at a rate of US $ 40.0011 00 bags up to 30-11-98. But on 13-10-98 the Corporation office at Harare in Sudan gave an offer to the Sudanese buyers at lower rate of US $ 38.67/100 bags FOB basis. The offer was made valid for October 1998 shipment and the workable letter of credit to reach by 23-10-98 violating the above term of the contract. Because of such offer and other reasons, the plaintiff suffered loss and it assessed the loss under different heads for breach of the contract and filed a final claim for US $ 1,806,816, to the Corporation as compensation. After negotiation, the Corporation addressed letters dated 14-5-2000 and 16-5-2000 to the plaintiff informing that under instruction of the Ministry it agreed to pay compensation of US $ 614,855.25 and further US $ 100,000 for loss of goodwill, in total US $ 714,855.25 towards full and final settlement of the claims. The plaintiff accepted the offer. Out of the said amount, the plaintiff deducted US $ 278,276.67 only from the invoices of scheduled jute mills of the Corporation but US $ 436,578.58 still remained outstanding. But the Corporation ultimately refused to pay any compensation as agreed and hence, the suit. 

 8. We have perused the revision application along with the contract, the plaint and other papers relied upon by the learned Advocate. The contract dated 29-9-98 as entered into by the parties is not disputed. It is also not disputed that the contract contains an arbitration agreement. The suit was instituted for recovery of compensation for breach of the contract, and damages incidental to and arising out of non-payment of such compensation. Case of the plaintiff is that it claimed compensation for US $ 1,806,816 for breach of the contract but after negotiations the defendant agreed to pay US$ 714,855.25 towards full and final settlement of all claims, which the plaintiff accepted. Out of the said amount, the firm deducted US $ 278,276.67 only from the invoices of scheduled jute mills of the Corporation but US $ 436,578.58 still remained outstanding. Now, the plaintiff seeks for a decree for that amount as well as further damages for non-payment of the remainder of the agreed compensation. Mr Rokanuddin Mahmud submits, the rights and obligations under the contract do no more subsist and consequently, the arbitration clause perishes along with the settlement. The claims in such suit are not based on the contract rather outside the terms of the contract and the arbitration clause. On the other hand, defendant has denied the settlement. Its case is that the above letters were obtained under the pressure of the then State Minister and without any concurrence of the Board of the Corporation. It is further claimed and steps have been already been taken to recover the amount as claimed by the plaintiff to have deducted from the invoices of different jute mills.
